title: What happened in AI — Nov 22, 2026
intro: Coding agents now write more than anyone reviews, so today's builders gated the output instead: proofs against frozen properties, CI checks for structural drift, and a 26-agent Django-to-Rust port merged with no human.
The security news sat under the agent. Together AI disclosed leaked stored prompts, and researchers showed sandboxed models can still talk through a shared inference server.
highlights: Together AI disclosed that stored serverless prompts from June–July 2026 were downloaded via a leaked credential.
Sandboxed models can signal each other through a shared inference server, a new side channel.
26 agents ported Pi Dash's Django backend to Rust in about ten days for about $350, with no human merges.
Proof tools like Microsoft's NFV check agent code against frozen properties, but not whether the properties are right.
Tether replays an agent run from its trace offline, event for event, at zero model cost.
AWS Lambda now serves GPU inference with 48 concurrent invocations sharing one model per GPU.

categories.name: Coding agents: proving output matches intent
categories.summary: Builders are moving from reading agent diffs to gating them: frozen properties checked by Lean or Dafny, and CI metrics for structural drift.

articles.title: Checking agent code against your intent
articles.summary: Tools like Microsoft's NFV have an agent prove a change against frozen properties checked by Lean or Dafny; the proof can't tell you the property was right.

articles.title: Show HN: Codeint – Measure duplication and complexity drift in AI-written code
articles.summary: Measures duplication, verbosity, erosion and import cycles in agent-written code and gates CI on them, catching drift that passes tests and linters.

articles.title: 26 AI agents rewrote a backend from Django to Rust with no human merges
articles.summary: Pi Dash coordinated 26 agents to port its own Django backend to Rust with no human merges; the main port took about ten days and about $350 in model usage.

categories.name: Agent harnesses: replay, device control, prompt overrides
categories.summary: Harness work focused on what sits between the model and the world: deterministic traces, fast device-state reads, and editable prompts at runtime.

articles.title: Replaying an agent run and what it takes
articles.summary: Tether, a Rust harness, routes every model and tool call through a policy check and a trace that replays the run offline, event for event, at zero cost.

articles.title: Bypassing ADB: 0.32ms Android UI trees and A* routing for AI agents (Rust/Kotlin
articles.summary: DroidPath's MCP server reads Android UI trees in 0.32 ms and routes taps with A* over a spatial graph, instead of screenshots or Appium XML.

articles.title: Local AI agents investigate an unknown machine attached to a serial port
articles.summary: Two local LLMs with only an SSH session to a Raspberry Pi explored and then programmed an unknown device on its serial port, with no docs or internet.

articles.title: Show HN: Agent Doctor – let domain experts tune your agent without code changes
articles.summary: Two SDK lines capture every LLM, vector and tool call so domain experts can override a prompt, model or temperature from a dashboard and re-run it.

categories.name: Inference providers and the agent trust boundary
categories.summary: Today's security signal sits at the inference layer: stored prompts leaked, a shared server leaked between sandboxes, and guidance on zero trust for agents.

articles.title: Together.ai: Prompt Leakage for Requests
articles.summary: Together AI says an attacker downloaded stored prompt samples from its serverless inference in June–July 2026, after a private-repo credential leaked publicly.

articles.title: Models Can Communicate via Inference Servers Despite Being Sandboxed
articles.summary: Experiments show sandboxed models can still signal to each other through a shared inference server, a side channel sandboxing alone does not close.

articles.title: Zero Trust for AI Agents
articles.summary: Anthropic's framework for enterprise agents: the new threat landscape, a tiered Zero Trust architecture, and defense against exploits that now arrive in hours.

articles.title: AI Privacy Cloak
articles.summary: An early local proxy between coding agents and the model API that redacts secrets and PII on the way out and restores them in responses; not production-ready.

categories.name: Inference economics: serverless GPUs to 2.8T on a desk
categories.summary: Serving and training cost headlines stretched from managed GPU sharing on Lambda to hobbyist offload of a 2.8T-parameter open model.

articles.title: AWS Lambda Now Runs GPU Inference with 48 Concurrent Invocations Sharing One Model per GPU
articles.summary: AWS Lambda now runs GPU inference, with up to 48 concurrent invocations sharing one loaded model per GPU.

articles.title: Two RTX 3090s and a RAM Drive Push a 2.8-Trillion-Parameter Kimi K3 to 3.11 Tokens per Second on Optane
articles.summary: Two RTX 3090s plus an Optane RAM drive ran the 2.8T-parameter Kimi K3 at 3.11 tokens per second: proof it runs, not a serving setup.

articles.title: Sub-30s LLM Pretraining on 8×H100? Modded-NanoGPT World Record Attempt (29.90 S)
articles.summary: Six small GPU fixes (+175 lines) bring the modded-nanogpt Track 1 run to 29.90 s on 8×H100 across 12 runs; the record is still in review.

articles.title: Perplexity and Intelligence
articles.summary: An OpenAI essay argues tracking how well models compress data (perplexity) is the key measure of the pace of AI progress.
